---
title: "018 — Image chat parts"
---

> **Status:** standing (idea 005's remaining modality slices — voice support, video
> support, files — stay recorded as future work, not abandoned)

**Goal.** Let users paste or attach an image into a chat whenever the connected model
supports vision, so Mayon finally exercises what multimodal models can do — until now the
composer and the server LLM path were text-only, so vision delivered none of its value
inside the app. The idea stage (ideas/005-multimedia-support, folded into spec
018-image-chat-parts) ruled a hybrid: Card 002's images-only scope — paste/attach with
capability gating — built under Card 001's extensibility contract, a parts-based message
architecture designed so every other modality becomes a follow-on slice rather than a
rewrite. Client-side compress/downsize before upload was day-one work; images live in the
primary store and ride the existing backup story; the vision gate stays advisory, failing
with clear errors rather than pretending to be omniscient.

**Why.** The recorded use case is vision-first — learning frontend engineering by sending
screenshots the model must see — which decided the idea deck: the files-as-text reframe
lost the bet ("the why is images the model can see"), and the voice-first and MCP-pull
cards were no-gos. Vision was judged roughly 90% of real demand; the hybrid delivers it in
a week or two while keeping Card 001's every-modality destination alive in the contract.

**Outcome & reversals.** Shipped in 0.6.0 (merged 2026-09-03, PR #24) with zero new
dependencies — downsizing uses the native Canvas API. The design holds every invariant by
construction rather than by patching: `content` remains the canonical flat text while a
nullable `parts` JSON-text column carries the ordered typed parts, so the generated
`search_vec` column keeps extracting message text with zero full-text-search changes,
guarded by a regression test; image bytes store as base64 data-URLs inside that same
column, riding pg_dump/restore untouched. Day-one downsizing (1568 px long edge, JPEG
q0.85, ≤500 KB target, passthrough for already-small images, first frame of animated GIFs)
runs before anything is stored or sent; two routes received a bounded 16 MiB `bodyLimit`
override because Fastify's 1 MiB default would have rejected downsized base64 payloads —
per-route widening following the backup-route precedent, not a global ceiling. The vision
gate follows the `toolCapability` precedent — `auto|on|off` over a static allowlist,
permissive-with-clear-error, never a hard block or runtime probing; the load-bearing
contract is preserved verbatim at
[appendices/018-provider-vision-flag.md](appendices/018-provider-vision-flag.md). Images
render outside the Markdown pipeline — the sanitize schema strips `data:` URIs, and
keeping parts out of markdown means zero expound/source-map interaction. A failed send
still leaves no row, since parts persist in the same single append as the text. No
reversals; the deliberate refusals — rewriting the search expression over JSON, a separate
blob store, chunked uploads — each traded an invariant for nothing at single-user scale.
Accepted deferred costs: image token weight is not estimated in context splitting (the
token-cost affordance is post-launch), and the manual full-quickstart validation pass was
left unticked at merge while all automated gates ran green. The idea stage's research
provenance now points at this page.

**Learnings.**

- Fold an idea's breadth into a contract, not a feature: parts-based messages made voice
  and video follow-on slices instead of a rewrite.
- Keep canonical text canonical: deriving search from the untouched text column held the
  full-text-search invariant by construction.
- Capability gates must be advisory when provider advertisement is fuzzy — a stale
  allowlist must still let a working model work, with a typed error instead of a provider
  dump.
- Widen only what must widen: bounded per-route limits absorb heavy payloads without a
  global ceiling or an upload protocol.
